title: Ser and estar
explanation:
Ser answers what something is. Estar answers where it is, or how it is right now. Soy Ana and soy de Madrid use ser. Estoy en Madrid and estoy bien use estar.

The same English verb to be covers both. The Spanish verb follows the meaning, not the English sentence.
commonMistake: Translating every to be as ser. Check whether the sentence is identity, origin, place, or a current condition.
